nodes.label: Protótipo de Alta Fidelidade — README
nodes.rationale: States the static HTML/Tailwind prototype (not Figma) is the official visual base meant to become Jinja2 templates directly, because it is more faithful to the plan's stack and immediately reusable in development.

nodes.label: RLS via SET LOCAL + JWT claims (per-transaction)
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated + set_config('request.jwt.claims', ...) injected per transaction lets RLS policies read auth.uid()/claims even under Supavisor transaction-mode pooling, because SET LOCAL is scoped to the transaction and does not leak across connections borrowed from the pool (a plain SET would).
nodes.norm_label: rls via set local + jwt claims (per-transaction)

nodes.label: Departamento-based routing model (2026-07-01 decision)
nodes.rationale: The portal is internal-only (no external paying tenants), so the isolation axis moves from empresa (company/tenant) to departamento: staff are scoped to their own department's queue, TI gains extra admin powers, and empresas/planos_sla survive only as internal SLA config plumbing (a single seeded org).

nodes.label: auth_is_ti() helper and its scope over time
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER helper that avoids RLS recursion when reading perfis; migration 0010 gave TI staff full read/write across all departments, but migration 0020 revoked the visibility/attend part, leaving TI equal to any other department for queue access and retaining only catalog/user/plan administration plus cross-department transfer.
nodes.norm_label: auth_is_ti() helper and its scope over time

nodes.label: SLA fallback ladder (contradiction C1)
nodes.rationale: Resolves a conflict between the briefing (flat 4h fallback) and the spec (12h/24h): the deadline resolves URGENTE = 50% of ALTA -> the company plan's configured value -> the plan's own default -> a global fallback of 12h response / 24h resolution when no plan is configured, discarding the briefing's 4h number.

nodes.label: Signed URL TTL policy for attachments (contradiction C2)
nodes.rationale: Storage attachment signed URLs use a 1-hour TTL regenerated on every server-side render; caching the signed URL beyond the TTL (session, cookie, Alpine state, or app memory) is explicitly forbidden, resolving the briefing's request for session-long caching in favor of the spec's 1h expiration.
nodes.norm_label: signed url ttl policy for attachments (contradiction c2)

nodes.label: Tailwind CLI build-step decision (contradiction C3)
nodes.rationale: Tailwind is compiled via CLI in the Dockerfile build stage and purged against the Jinja templates rather than loaded from CDN at runtime, because the Tailwind CDN runtime is incompatible with the strict production CSP and with purging; CDN is allowed only in development.

nodes.label: Alpine.js CSP build requirement
nodes.rationale: Production CSP forbids unsafe-eval, so the standard Alpine.js build (which uses eval/Function) is blocked; the CSP build is mandatory and restricts expressions to named component methods/properties, banning complex inline JS in x-data.

nodes.label: service_role key exclusion policy
nodes.rationale: service_role bypasses RLS by design, so it must never serve user data or reach the browser; domain queries go through asyncpg with per-transaction JWT claims (option B) instead of a service_role+empresa_id-filter-everywhere approach (option C), which was rejected as fragile because it depends on 100% query discipline.

nodes.label: Realtime chat topology decision
nodes.rationale: The browser connects directly to Supabase Realtime via supabase-js instead of a FastAPI WS/SSE bridge, because a bridge would duplicate state and add a bottleneck; FastAPI stays the sole write path (validates CSRF/permission/is_interna) while Realtime only delivers already-persisted rows, with 5s HTMX polling as fallback if the socket destabilizes.

nodes.label: Migration 0020 — TI scope restriction
nodes.rationale: Reverted only the visibility/attend branch of auth_is_ti() introduced by 0010: TI staff now see/attend only their own department's tickets like any other department; TI keeps catalog/user/plan administration and cross-department transfer. A bug fixed in the 2026-07-08 session came from code still assuming the pre-0020 'TI sees everything' behavior.

nodes.label: Migrations 0027/0028 — Setor unificado + Líder de setor
nodes.rationale: Unifies 'Setor' (origin department of any employee) with 'Departamento' (ticket destination) into one catalog; adds departamentos.recebe_chamados to mark which departments can be a ticket destination, and grants an ADMIN in a non-queue department ('líder de setor') read-only visibility over tickets opened by their own team, even when routed elsewhere — without changing who can update/attend.
nodes.norm_label: migrations 0027/0028 — setor unificado + lider de setor
